decisions.reason: 뜻밖이었다 is a surprise; simple past reads more naturally than past-perfect “had been unexpected.”
걸리는 사실 is a nagging/troubling fact, not a sudden memory.
Links the week off to possible Sangdong trouble, matching the 건 아니죠 check without blaming Choi personally.
아니 왜 plus 문제 is colloquial “you know… the whole thing,” not a formal “situation.”
끝난다고 해서요 is reported “supposed to,” and 리모델링 is remodeling, not a settled “will be renovated.”
The question is general (경우도 있나 about remodeling), not this Guild’s current renovation.
좋긴 한데 is concessive after the skepticism; “Still” keeps that beat.
앞만 보고 달려온 is the forward-staring, running-life image; “push forward” drops it.
이럴 때일수록 더욱 is “even harder at times like this,” not merely “precisely when.”
아 and 휴가지만 are Choi’s comic pivot after “I want to work”; SOL drops them.
“Need” and “have to” are indistinguishable for 가야 해서.
……네 is a stunned “Yes,” not “All right.”
“Hurried over” is tighter English for 다가와 with the same 종종걸음 haste.
되었사옵니다 is stilted perfective “has been prepared,” and the Korean has no “your.”
“Stop talking like that” is more natural Taekyung for 그 말투 그만해.
유료 결제 is a paid purchase/IAP, not an “upgrade.”
어렵게도 한다 is the roundabout method of asking, not making it “sound” complicated.
씩 웃는다 is a grin; BASE’s “wide” is unsupported.
맛있대 is present hearsay (“Mom says… is”), not past “said/was.”
늘 only modifies 새로워; repeating “always” three times rewrites the catchphrase rhythm, and 배신 is “lets you down.”
Keeps the Korean’s paired nominal snapshot instead of turning it into two copular clauses.
휴가가 별거냐 is “what’s so special,” not “who needed a fancy vacation.”
전화가 끊긴 스마트폰 must stay; SOL drops that the call had just ended.
Keep the separate quote; the SOL merge is the same line that already omitted the ended-call detail.
안 그래도 is “already/as it happens,” not “worried too.”
Thinking-scene 두드렸다 is repeated tapping; “drummed” is the natural English gesture.
Need both 지금도 and 존재; BASE drops “even now,” SOL replaces existence with “the man.”
decisions.replacement: Even now, some time after Jin Taekyung’s sudden appearance, his existence remained a mystery.

decisions.reason: 쓸어 버렸다 is “swept through,” not generic “cleared an entire.”
바뀌었다 is “turned into”; naming Minwoo is unnecessary extra specificity.
Keeps the two-sentence punch of 그것도 매우 빠르게; “astonishing rate” over-formalizes it.
없습니까 / 추가 정보 is a formal negative “no additional information,” not “any new.”
재확인을 거듭 is repeated reconfirmation, not a generic “checked.”
신중하게 입을 뗐다 is carefully opening his mouth to speak, not “chose his words.”
찾아볼 is look for/find cases of an unheard-of type, not “look into” known ones.
듣도 보도 못한 is never heard or seen, and 않았을 것이다 is counterfactual “would have used.”
Preserves the 재각성 tautology and 그다음이 없기 without adding “precisely” or “stage.”
그건. is a trailing fragment; SOL’s “would” is not in the Korean.
난색을 표하다 is showing reluctance, not preparing to “explain the difficulty.”
산증인 is a living witness, not “living proof”; 참전했다 is participated in battles.
시선에도 / 특별했다 is “even to his eyes… special,” not “exceptional.”
강하게 is forceful manner, and 공수 전환 is efficient offense-defense transitions, not merely “powerful” shifting.
Same 압도적-only thought, cleaner English without the extra “when he watched” frame.
3차 각성자라. is musing “huh,” not a bare ellipsis.
시간은 걸리겠지만 is “it would take time,” not already “the investigation”; 알아볼 가치 is worth investigating.
고개 숙였다 to the Young Master is a bow of assent.
동향 is intelligence “movements”; “up to” is too casual for Choi, and 아 is “Ah.”
감시원들을 풀었습니다 / 입수할 matches formal “deployed surveillance agents… obtain,” not “sent out watchers… have.”
달라붙기 시작했다 is already latching on, and 반나절도 되지 않았는데 is “not even half a day.”
겠군요 is inferential “must be,” more natural than a stiff “then.”
Restores 샅샅이 and 일단은 as starting with a thorough guild-wide analysis.
해 두었습니다 is present perfect, and 붙을 수도 있으니 is “in case,” not a statement that they might be followed.
Keep the hesitation beat; SOL only deletes it to merge a later “warn” rewrite.
알려 줘야 is tell/inform, not “warn.”
훨씬 뛰어났으면 is “far superior” in this formal register, not merely “better.”
가장 많은 것이 드러나 있는 is how much has been revealed, not a life “laid bare.”
맑은 샘물을 보면서 is looking at clear spring water, not “staring” into a “crystal-clear” spring.
빌려서라도 is “even if,” and 정체 is true identity; BASE weakens -라도, SOL drops 정체.
decisions.replacement: Even if it meant using Sangdong Guild’s power, Choi Minwoo wanted to get closer to Jin Taekyung’s true identity.

decisions.reason: 났나 봅니다 is “it seems,” and 화가 단단히 is thoroughly angry, not “must be furious.”
신중해진 / 예전 같았으면 is “grown more cautious; in the old days,” cleaner than “if this were the past.”
아, 혹시? is “Ah. Could it be?” not “Wait” plus an added ellipsis.
Same 반응에 웃으며 끄덕였다, more natural English word order.
안면이 있습니다 is being acquainted, not a single “I’ve met before.”
악연 is an ill-fated relationship, not one “bad encounter.”
SOL drops 내가 대답했다 and invents “under the lights.”
집 좀 보려고요 is generic “a house,” more natural than “some houses.”
월세/전세/아니면 lists housing types as nouns; mixing “rent monthly” with “jeonse lease” breaks the parallel.
매매요 as spoken English is “I’m buying,” completing the type list.
이것만 처리하고 후딱 올게 is take care of this and be right back; SOL drops the return and turns 이것 into “something.”
뭘 처리하나 is what he needed to take care of, not a metafictional *something*.
다른 것도 아니고 그거면 supplies the “definitely hurry” emphasis in Taekyung’s voice.
뭐라도 드시면서 is “have something to eat,” not specifically a snack.
푸드득 matches “Pfft” as the chapter’s unitalicized SFX; “Prrt” is a different sound.
Same 못 먹겠군, more natural contracted narration.
이미 틀어져 있던 TV is already on; SOL omits that.
정체불명 is unidentified, not merely mysterious.
초췌한 is haggard, not exhausted; tighter newsreel cadence.
뿐만이 아닌 is “not only,” and the trimmed parallel is still complete.
게이트는 말 그대로 문을 뜻한다 must define Gate, and 군단 is an army, not a horde.
교과서에 적힌 대로 is “as written in the textbooks,” not “as the textbooks said.”
Keeps the place-list then 때와 장소를 가리지 않고, and 살인과 파괴 as murder and destruction, not “death.”
Makes 게이트가 열린 후… 끝났을 때 unambiguous: Bloody Week began with the Gates and the toll is at its end.
가장 끔찍했던 10년의 역사 is one horrific ten-year span, not “the ten most horrific years.”
자막과 함께 must stay; SOL drops the caption.
이제 좀 살겠네 is “now I feel alive,” without BASE’s extra “again.”
털썩 주저앉았다 is a comic plop, not “dropped heavily into his seat.”
들렀다가 is “stop by,” more accurate than “visit.”
그으래요? is elongated “Really?” not “Is that so?”
눈동자를 굴리는 is rolling his eyes, and 호구 is a sucker; BASE has fool, SOL has darted.
decisions.replacement: Judging by the way his eyes rolled around, he seemed to be deciding whether or not to take me for a sucker. I pretended not to notice and held out the note I had prepared.

decisions.reason: Both only restate that the address is on the note; no gain.
이쪽 매물 is property around this address/area, not “the property at this address.”
안전 구역인데 is that the address is in a safe zone.
매매 맞죠 is “you really said buy, right?”; “definitely” over-sharpens it.
위아래로 움직인다 is a once-over; adding “my body” is extra body-part specification.
있어 보이는 차림 is “dressed like a man with money,” more spoken than “someone wealthy.”
게이트 뜁니다 is the “run Gates” idiom, not glossary “raid.”
젊은 분이 성공하셨네 is idiomatic “done well at such a young age.”
웃음꽃이 활짝 피었다 is a smile blossoming, and 고수입 직종 is high-income profession, not “best-paid around.”
한결 친절해진 말투로 물었다 is asking in a much friendlier tone; SOL adds “immediately” and drops “asked.”
시세 as market prices is the established listing; singular is not an improvement.
검색해 봤어요 is searched, not “looked it up.”
안 그래도 매물이 좀 있긴 is “actually happen to be”; SOL drops 안 그래도.
몸이 달았는지 is hedged “perhaps,” not a stated “eager to close a sale.”
Same hang-up-and-redial five minutes, cleaner single sentence.
어떻게… 보실래요 is “how about we go see it,” matching the tag 어떻게.
함박웃음을 지었다 is “beamed”; tighter vacation-so-no-reason line.
승용차 조수석 keeps the sedan; SOL omits the car.
곁눈질했다 is a sidelong glance, not a plain glance.
어릴 때요 is casual “when I was a kid,” matching Taekyung to the agent.
고향인 셈이다 is “in a way,” not “I supposed.”
많이 바뀌었을 is “pretty different,” not “completely different.”
Same jeonse spike and move, cleaner cause-and-effect without calqued “I already knew that.”
Inner-thought 아버지 matches the chapter’s “Mom” as “Dad.”
숨죽여 우시는 is crying silently (suppressed sound), not merely “in silence.”
몇 년이나 / 그곳 / 신혼집 is several years later, the place, newlywed home—not “years later,” “apartment,” or “first home.”
정신을 차렸다 from the memory is being pulled out of his thoughts; smoother arrival beat.
후딱 보고 나오자고 is “have a quick look and be on our way,” more natural than “get going.”
잠시만요 is “just a moment,” equally natural; “hold on” is mere synonym churn.
과거의 향수 is nostalgia, and 어딘지 모르게 친숙하다 is strangely familiar; each candidate keeps only one.
decisions.replacement: Maybe it was nostalgia. The old apartment complex had already been demolished, but the area still felt strangely familiar.

decisions.reason: “Hasn’t changed completely” vs “hasn’t completely changed” is indistinguishable for 아주 바뀌진 않아서.
입맛을 다셨다 is smacking his lips, not clicking his tongue, and 옛 풍경 is old scenery.
좋으신가 / 이참에 / 한 바퀴 is happy, while you’re at it, a lap—not “enjoying yourself,” “while you’re here,” or a generic walk.
아니에요? is “aren’t you?” after 거잖아.
이 집은 어떻게든 사야 한다 is direct “I had to buy this house”; BASE pads it.
피식 웃은 is a short chuckle, not a “quiet laugh.”
신경 쓰지 말고 다녀와요 is “don’t worry about me,” not “take your time”; 편의 봐 is accommodate.
천천히 걷기 시작했다 is began walking slowly, not a “leisurely” set-off.
발견한 is spotted/found; “spotted” is the sharper verb for the same beat.
The overheard line addresses 오빠; BASE makes it first-person “I,” SOL still claims “my hangout.”
decisions.replacement: “Oppa, this used to be your hangout when you were a kid. Back when you smoked like crazy in middle school, the old lady here was so old that…”

decisions.reason: 슈퍼 앞에 is in front of the supermarket; SOL’s “outside” and “beside it” are unsupported.
Same 갸웃거리던… 다가와 말했다 plus the question, cleaner as one sentence.
Accept the merge; the quote is already in the previous SOL sentence.
